tools.description: Write a published lesson the shared player can open. Pass slug plus worksheet. worksheet is the object assigned to window.WORKSHEET: title, level (basic|intermediate|advanced), optional activities array, and any of vocab, fill, grammar, reading, askFriend. activities is an ordered path of steps, each { type, ...fields }. Call list_activity_types for the catalog. Omit activities and the player builds a default path from the sections that exist. Lesson rules: the story is most of the lesson, written with vowel points, new words wrapped in { word }, and reading.retell cues for round 2. grammar.rules holds exactly one pattern; extra points go in grammar.reminders as one-liners. Bring back 3 to 5 earlier words with from (see list_words). Every speaking question has pointed Hebrew. Level defaults: basic = 3 choices and open word bank; intermediate = 4 choices and closed bank; advanced = typing allowed and shorter timers. Vowels stay on with a manual toggle. Do not add root/binyan speed drills. Audio: after a successful write, the server generates ElevenLabs clips automatically (words, vocab sentences, story lines, grammar pointed lines, speaking and comprehension questions). Do not write audio, sentenceAudio, or reading.audio fields yourself — omit them. Words are cached under _audio/words and reused across lessons (never regenerated). Pass audio:false to skip generation. Visibility (optional): "everyone" or { users: ["username", ...] }. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. Unknown usernames fail before any write. Omit on a new lesson to keep it hidden; omit on an existing lesson to leave visibility unchanged. From a class call: pick the story, 8 to 12 words, one pattern, 3 to 5 recycled words, then an activity mix by level. Never put the transcript or the learner name in the lesson. The tool sets id to the slug, copies worksheets/_template/index.html when the folder is new, updates worksheets/catalog.js (or LESSONS_DIR), and runs the project validator. A failed check restores the previous files. Warnings do not block the write; fix them. Audio failures do not roll back the lesson.

audio.description: Generate ElevenLabs audio after a successful write. Defaults to true. Pass false to skip.

blurb.description: One line under the card on the home page.

slug.description: New folder name: lowercase words separated by hyphens.

visibility.description: Optional. "everyone" or { users: ["username", ...] }. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. Omit to leave new lessons hidden and existing lessons unchanged.

worksheet.description: Lesson object: title, level, activities, plus vocab, fill, grammar, reading, askFriend sections to include.

slug.description: Lesson folder name, such as shai-date-indirect-speech.

tools.description: Generate or relink audio for an existing published lesson. Words are shared under _audio/words and never overwritten; existing word files are reused across lessons. Sentences, story lines, grammar pointed lines, and questions regenerate only when their text changes, or when forceSentences is true. Use after backfilling an older lesson, or when upsert_lesson was called with audio:false.

forceSentences.description: Regenerate sentence/story/grammar/question clips even when text is unchanged. Never regenerates words.

tools.title: Generate ElevenLabs audio for a lesson

tools.description: Read the plan part at an id path. An empty path is the plan document. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. Returns the part, the current revision, and editState. editState lists the fields at or below that path that a person last changed (path, field, revision, previousValue, previousWriter), and lastHumanEdit is the newest person edit anywhere in the plan. It is advice: you may edit those fields anyway, and the note never blocks a write. If you overwrite one, your write result lists it in overwrote, and restore_plan_revision puts the person's value back. Read a part before you edit it. Use list_plans to find a plan id and create_plan to start one. Does not change the plan.

path.description: Id path such as units/unit-1/lessons/cafe-order/blocks/introduction/words/2. Empty string is the whole plan.

tools.name: read_part
tools.title: Read one part of a lesson plan

tools.description: Draft an English meaning for every word in a graded-story block that has no gloss yet. Pass the plan id and the id path of the block, for example units/unit-1/lessons/cafe-order/blocks/story. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. The meanings come from the app dictionary and are a first draft: some are the base word of a form (form says which), some are a different sense from the one the story uses, and unmatched lists words with no entry. Read each one against the story, fix it, then save the whole map with set_field on the block (field glosses, at most 80 words). A reader sees these meanings when they tap a word, so a wrong one teaches the wrong thing. Does not change the plan.

path.description: Id path of a graded-story block.

tools.name: suggest_glosses
tools.title: Draft word meanings for a graded story

tools.description: Make (or reuse) the spoken clip for up to 20 Hebrew words and return each word's audioPath. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. Pass the words as written in the plan, with vowel points: the clip is for that exact spelling, and points are what make the voice say it right. A word that already has a clip is reused and costs nothing; a new one is made once with ElevenLabs and kept for every lesson, never overwritten. This does not change a plan: save each audioPath with set_field on the word entry (field audioPath). Words with no clip and an error (not_configured, bad_word, failed) are listed in the same order.

words.description: Hebrew words, with vowel points, as in the plan.

tools.name: make_word_audio

tools.description: Replace the part at an id path. Pass path, value, and expectedRevision. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN. The value's id must equal the id in the path (id_mismatch otherwise), and audience and assigneeId cannot change here (assign_required; use assign_plan). A stale expectedRevision returns revision_conflict and the stored revision, and writes nothing. The result lists overwrote when you replaced a field a person last wrote; restore_plan_revision puts it back.

expectedRevision.description: Revision from the last read. Must match the stored working copy.

path.description: Id path of the part to replace. Empty string replaces the plan document.

It is refused when a check finds a block (list_plan_issues shows them, validation lists them) or when the plan uses a picture that is still pending approval in a lesson visible to learners (pending_media). A stale expectedRevision returns revision_conflict and the stored revision. Nothing is written when it is refused. A lesson is visible only if its visibility is everyone or selected; a new lesson is hidden.

Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

expectedRevision.description: Revision from the last read. Must match the stored working copy.

tools.description: List every lesson plan: id, title, audience, status, revision, updatedAt, published, unpublishedChanges, and humanEditedFields. Call this first to find a plan id. Newest update first, at most 200 (truncated says there are more). published means a snapshot exists and learners can read it; unpublishedChanges means the working copy is ahead of that snapshot. humanEditedFields counts the fields a person last changed. If it is above 0, read_part shows them in editState. No assignee name is returned, only assigned (true or false). Does not change anything. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

limit.description: At most this many plans. Default and maximum 200.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.title: List lesson plans

tools.description: Make a new draft plan at revision 1 from a title and an optional recipe. Omit id: the server assigns a UUID. An id you pass must already be a lowercase slug. An id that exists returns already_exists and nothing is changed or overwritten. recipe is one of topic-conversation, review-worksheet, verse-reading, verb-workshop, letters-and-vowels, guide. It sets the lesson recipe and nothing else. unitId and lessonId are optional slugs for the one unit and one lesson made for you (default unit-1 and lesson-1). A part id cannot be renamed later, so pick them now. The new plan is shared, its lesson is hidden, and it has one placeholder block (id placeholder, type fluency-pass). It holds no Hebrew. Next: read_part with an empty path to get the revision, insert your real blocks with insert_block, then remove the placeholder with remove_block (a lesson must keep at least one block). A draft is invisible to learners until publish_plan. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

id.description: Omit this. The server assigns a UUID. Pass one only to retry an id you already chose.

lessonId.description: Optional id of the first lesson. Default lesson-1.

title.description: Plan title as plain text, no markup.

unitId.description: Optional id of the first unit. Default unit-1.

tools.name: create_plan
tools.title: Create a lesson plan

tools.description: List the revisions of one plan, newest first: revision, op, path, field, summary, actorKind, actorName, tool, at. actorKind is ai, human, or system. A person's revisions show actorName human, never a name. Use sinceRevision with the revision you last read to see what was written after it, and actorKind human to see only what a person changed. pathPrefix keeps revisions whose path starts with that text. limit defaults to 50 and is at most 200; truncated says there are more, so pass beforeRevision with the oldest revision shown to page back. A summary never holds a field value. Use get_plan_revision for the whole plan at one revision, or diff_plan for what changed. Does not change anything. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

actorKind.description: Only revisions written by this kind of actor.

beforeRevision.description: Only revisions before this one. For paging.

pathPrefix.description: Only revisions whose path starts with this text.

tools.name: list_plan_revisions
tools.title: List the revision history of a plan

tools.description: Read the whole plan document as it was at one revision, with that revision's metadata. Use it to see an old value before you restore it. It does not change the plan or the revision counter. not_found means the plan or that revision does not exist. A plan that has not been written since history began has no rows before its first edit. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: get_plan_revision
tools.title: Read a plan as it was at one revision

tools.description: List what changed between two points of one plan. from and to are each a revision number, working (the draft now), or published (the last snapshot learners read). Example: from published to working is everything not yet published. from 5 to working is everything since revision 5. Each entry has path, field, kind (changed, added, removed, or moved), before, after. path is an id path you can pass to read_part, set_field, or restore_plan_revision. Pass path to keep one part and what is under it. truncated true means the list was cut: narrow it with path. no_snapshot means the plan was never published. Does not change anything. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

path.description: Id path: keep only this part and what is under it.

tools.name: diff_plan
tools.title: Diff a plan between two revisions

tools.description: Put an older revision back as a NEW revision. History is kept and nothing is erased, so a restore can itself be restored. Pass fromRevision and expectedRevision (the revision you last read). With only those, the whole plan comes back. With path, one part comes back. With path and field, one field comes back (path is empty for a field of the plan itself). Workflow: list_plan_revisions or diff_plan to find the revision and the id path, get_plan_revision if you want to see the old value, then restore_plan_revision with the narrowest path and field that fits. Use it to undo your own mistake, or to put back a value a person had set (editState and overwrote name that revision). Cannot change who a personal plan is assigned to: audience and assigneeId stay as they are (a field restore of either returns assign_required; use assign_plan). The draft keeps its status draft; learners keep reading the last published snapshot until you publish_plan. A stale expectedRevision returns revision_conflict and the stored revision, and writes nothing. The restored plan is validated like any write; a refusal lists the reasons and writes nothing. not_found carries a reason when the part cannot be placed back (parent_missing or absent_in_revision). Your result includes overwrote when the restore replaced a field a person last wrote. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

expectedRevision.description: Revision from the last read. Must match the stored working copy.

field.description: One field of that part. Omit to restore the whole part.

path.description: Id path of one part. Omit to restore the whole plan.

tools.name: restore_plan_revision
tools.title: Restore a plan, one part, or one field from a revision

tools.description: List what the checks find in the draft of one plan, with a stable code, severity, path, field, message, and a fix where one is known. severity block is a hard error: it stops publish_plan. warn is advice and never stops a write or a publish. By default you get block and warn; pass inform or all to see more. counts always covers the whole plan. Codes include pointing-form, field-language, lexicon-form, pointing-consistency, and audio-stale, plus the older rules. A fix is { action, path, field, suggested } where action is set_field or replace_part: apply it with that tool, or choose your own repair. path is an id path for read_part and set_field. pointer is the raw JSON pointer. Call this after you build or change a plan and before publish_plan, then fix what you can. Does not change anything. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

pathPrefix.description: Only issues at or under this id path.

severity.description: block, warn, inform, all, or a list of them. Default block and warn.

tools.name: list_plan_issues
tools.title: List the problems the checks find in a plan

tools.description: Set who a plan is for. audience is shared (every learner who may see its lessons) or personal (one learner). For personal pass assigneeId, the username of an active account (see list_users). For shared leave assigneeId out. Pass expectedRevision, the revision you last read. This is the only way to change audience or assigneeId: set_field, replace_part, and restore_plan_revision cannot. assignee_refused means that account is unknown or disabled; nothing was written. A stale expectedRevision returns revision_conflict and the stored revision. Learners see a plan only after publish_plan. A personal plan is shown only to its assignee. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

assigneeId.description: Username of an active account. Required for personal.

expectedRevision.description: Revision from the last read. Must match the stored working copy.

tools.name: assign_plan
tools.title: Assign a plan to everyone or to one learner

tools.description: Read one learner's progress summary while you draft their next lesson. Call it only for that learner. planning_off means an admin has not turned AI planning on: stop, do not retry, and do not invent a profile. The profile has no glosses. Use get_lexicon_entry for a word's meaning. Never paste the profile, or any part of it, into a lesson file, a worksheet, or a saved plan. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: get_learner_profile
tools.title: Read a learner profile

tools.description: Score a Hebrew text against one learner's library before you use it as a reading. text is at most 4000 characters. The result names unknown tokens from that text. planning_off means AI planning is off for that learner: nothing was scored. Never paste the learner profile into a lesson file. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

text.description: Hebrew text to score. At most 4000 characters are accepted.

tools.name: check_text_coverage
tools.title: Check known-word coverage

tools.description: List the grammar concepts the player tracks: key, family, and labels. Call this when a lesson or a drill needs a concept id. This is not learner data. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: list_grammar_concepts
tools.title: List grammar concepts

tools.description: Search lexicon entries by gloss, part of speech, binyan, tense, or root class. Call this before you cite a word or add it to a learner's library. Unverified forms are included. You cannot mark a form verified. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

cursor.description: Key of the last entry on the previous page.

pos.description: Part of speech, such as noun or verb.

verified.description: Filter by the person's verified flag. You cannot change it.

tools.name: list_lexicon
tools.title: Search the lexicon

tools.description: Read one lexicon entry by its exact key, with its lemma and paradigm. Call this to join a profile word_id to a gloss. The profile itself must not be pasted into a lesson file. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

key.description: Lexicon key, the same string as a profile word_id.

tools.name: get_lexicon_entry
tools.title: Read one lexicon entry

tools.description: Write lexicon entries. Call this before add_library_words when a key is not in the lexicon yet. Rows are stored with source mcp. A verified field on an entry is ignored: you cannot mark a form verified. Pass expectedRev 0 for a new key, or the current rev when you edit. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: upsert_lexicon_entries
tools.title: Write lexicon entries

tools.description: Add lexicon keys to one learner's library so they can review them. planning_off means AI planning is off: nothing was written. Every key must already be a lexicon entry. unknown_keys means the whole call was refused; write those entries with upsert_lexicon_entries first, then retry. At most 50 new words per learner per local day. Never paste the learner profile into a lesson file. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: add_library_words
tools.title: Add lexicon words to a learner library

tools.description: Do not call. Marking a form verified is a person's act, done by an admin. This tool always returns forbidden and writes nothing. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: set_lexicon_verified
tools.title: Mark a lexicon form verified

tools.description: Do not call. Only an admin can change AI planning, from the admin page. This tool always returns forbidden and does not change the switch. Requires MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.
tools.name: set_ai_planning
tools.title: Change the AI-planning switch
